title: Garrett Hardin's 'Tragedy of the Commons' (1968)
explainer: Hardin's 1968 Science essay described how a resource shared by many users without any enforced limits gets over-exploited, because each user has an individual incentive to take more while the cost of depletion is spread across everyone. A maintainer's time, review bandwidth, and a project's CI budget are exactly this kind of shared resource, and maintainer burnout is a modern instance of the overgrazed commons.

title: Elinor Ostrom and How Commons Actually Get Governed (1990)
explainer: Two decades after Hardin, political economist Elinor Ostrom's field studies of real irrigation systems and fisheries showed that shared resources are routinely managed successfully, not through privatization or a central authority, but through communities that build their own enforced rules: contribution norms, monitoring, and graduated consequences for people who don't follow them. That is a close model for what a healthy maintainer team actually does with CONTRIBUTING guides, review gates, and project norms, and it's why Ostrom shared the 2009 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences, becoming the first woman to win it.
